newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: VA Stahl more optimistic on 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: VA Stahl more optimistic on 1997/98.

text.p: Austrian steelmaker VA Stahl on Monday reported a group net profit of 643 million schillings in the three months to March 31 and announced it would pay a three schillings per share dividend for the period.
VA Steel, which has switched its financial year to end on March 31 instead of December 31, said in a statement it was confident its results in 1997/8 would at least match 1996.

"The marked economic upturn in the European Union permits a somewhat more optimistic prognosis for the short-term development of the steel market than was possible at the turn of the year," the company said, pointing to higher prices and rising demand.
VA Stahl shares jumped to an intra-day high of 550 schillings on the statement, 10 up on the day. Earlier the stock had been trading at 541 schillings.
In the "short year" to March 31, group pretax profit reached 741 million schillings on sales of 7.9 billion. No comparative figures were available.
For the full-year 1996 VA Stahl reported a net profit of 1.688 billion schillings and sales of 31.519 billion. It paid a 12 schillings per share dividend.
The firm forecast a five percent increase in quarterly contract prices between the second and third quarters of 1997 but added the group would not let up in its cost-cutting drive.
"The target...is the identification of cost-cutting potential of around 500 million schillings annually," it said.
The group said it remained open to a strategic cooperation in central and eastern Europe, providing VA Stahl assumed the industrial leadership.
